transitive_call_effects.evidence: Pinned context disassembly in original-disassembly.md: 283E:000A sets DX=0x388, loads byte register/value arguments and calls 283E:0020. That helper outputs register to 0x388, polls input 0x388 in fixed 10-iteration and 40-iteration LOOPs, outputs value to 0x389, and returns; each direct call therefore causes two byte OUTs and 50 status INs. Poll status is not used to choose an f_2815_0165 branch. This describes the transitive I/O contract, not additional branch_map entries for the target.

reads: BP+0x06 signed word instr; BP+0x08 signed word note; BP+0x0a signed word vol; BP+0x0c signed word voice.
Far signed word fd_50F6_4B16; fd_50F6_0000[instr] using 6-byte entries and far pointer member at +2; instrument bytes p[2], signed word *(int far *)(p+0x0d), signed word *(int far *)(p+0x0b).
Far table fd_55B3_6BA4[vol] as the low byte of each 2-byte element; byte tables g_6908[voice], g_6912[g_6908[voice]], and word table g_6924[remainder] (low and high bytes for the two pitch writes).
Transitive helper reads status port 0x388 for its fixed delay loops; target function does not inspect those values.
writes: BP+0x08 note argument slot receives the 16-bit transposed note before the signed range check. This is transient caller argument-area state under the far-call ABI.
Frame temporaries store the far instrument pointer at BP-8/BP-6 and the saved voice word at BP-0xa; saved SI/DI/BP and call argument stack space are restored/unwound.
No instrument/table/global memory is written. Observable device effects are only the ordered f_283E_000A calls and their transitive 0x388/0x389 I/O.
memory_state.global_state: No global data mutation and no return value (void far). The input vol value is held in DI for clamp/index use; original code does not overwrite BP+0xa.

constants_widths_pointer_arithmetic.widths_signedness: MSC target int is signed 16-bit. Initial volume additions, clamps, instrument transposition multiply-by-12 and note update are word operations interpreted signed by JNS/JLE/JS/JG. The attenuation multiply is unsigned 16-bit: operands are in 0..63 so product <=3969 and no product truncation changes the value; SHR 6 is logical. Table values and masks are then reduced to the low byte passed to the char helper ABI.
constants_widths_pointer_arithmetic.pointer_math: instr indexes 6-byte Instr records; the far pointer is loaded from member offset +2. p+0x0d and p+0x0b are byte-offset far accesses to signed words; p[2] is an unsigned byte. The volume lookup uses element stride 2 (int table) and the low byte. note%12 and note/12 are evaluated only on the 0..127 signed range, so signed IDIV remainder/quotient equal the C source operations.
constants_widths_pointer_arithmetic.constants: Volume clamps 0 and 0x7f; attenuation uses 0x3f and shift 6, preserving p[2] upper mask 0xc0; note transposition multiplier 12; note bounds 0..0x7f; semitone divisor/table length 12; pitch register bases 0xa0/0xb0 and octave offset 8; operator-volume register base 0x40.
